hook.text: Two newspapers cover the same protest. One headline says 'Peaceful March.' The other says 'Streets in Chaos.'

buildup.text: Media bias is the systematic slanting of news coverage in favor of or against particular perspectives.

discovery.text: Bias can appear in story selection, word choice, source selection, placement, and omission of information.

twist.text: Complete objectivity is impossible. Every editorial choice — what to cover and how — involves judgment.

climax.text: The goal isn't bias-free media. It's recognizing bias when you see it and consuming accordingly.

punchline.text: All media has a perspective. The question is whether it's transparent about it.

quiz.question: In what ways can media bias manifest?
options: Story selection, word choice, source selection, placement, and omission
